summary.oneLiner: the *lower end* of the company's own 26, *"we have definitely seen the bottom in the first quarter itself"*

one-line thesis: SBI Life opened FY27 with Individual Rated Premium of ₹39.7bn (+14% YoY) and VoNB of ₹14.1bn (+29%), holding its
22.2% private IRP market share — but reported VoNB margin fell to 26.2%, the lower end of the company's own
26–28% guidance band, because of two explicitly-named drags: an unusually large one-off Group Term Insurance
(GTI) win that inflated total APE to ₹53.8bn (+36%) at group-level margins, and the residual GST hit of
₹2.3bn. Management called the margin bottom — "we have definitely seen the bottom in the first quarter
itself" — and the underlying mix story is genuinely improving: ULIP down to 62% of IRP, pure protection +41%,
agency +20% and non-SBI banks +31% on APE, so the FY27 question is whether individual mix normalisation carries
margin back toward the 28% upper band once GST annualises on 22-Sep-2026.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > All figures exactly as stated on the call. Nothing computed here; ratios/margins are management's own.
Product mix — individual APE / IRP (as stated):
Sum assured & riders: individual NB sum assured +46%, group NB sum assured +265%; rider sum assured now
39% of individual sum assured; protection-segment individual sum assured +40%.
> Adjustments / one-offs — called out explicitly:
> 1. GTI one-off (₹12.3bn group protection APE, +313%) — treated as regular premium, not single premium:
>    "There is a 1-year renewable contract. We always consider our new premium as APE." It is the sole cause of
>    the −60 bps product-mix drag on VoNB margin: "You're understanding right on the 60 basis points of
>    product mix is concerned. This is only on account of the GTI." Management refused to size the contract:
>    "we do not comment on individual contracts or individual policies."
> 2. GST — ₹2.3bn, 1.1 pp of margin. Prior-quarter drags cited by the analyst were ~1.1 pp (Q3) and 1.5 pp (Q4).
> 3. Assumption change −40 bps in the VoNB walk is a BASE EFFECT, not a Q1 action: "in this quarter, we have
>    not made any change in assumption. And as part of annual review, we made the assumption change in March '26.
>    Since we are showing this walk from the June last year to this year, that's why impact is coming."
>    Management added the March review was itself "negative by 20 basis points" on operating assumptions.
> 4. Stamp duty spike in other expenses — "that is one-off item, which has been the impact in the first quarter."
> 5. Labour-code employee-cost impact — "this is the first quarter where we have seen this impact."
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: IRP growth (the company's headline KPI): "our growth projections for the year on IRP basis remains at 14%,
15%." Management framed Q1 as delivered: "we have delivered what we had promised around 14%, 15% growth and
our IRP growth is in that range."
VoNB margin: 26%–28% band reaffirmed, with an explicit call that Q1 was the trough — "The margin guidance
was 26% to 28%, and we are within the range, although at the lower end of that" … "we have definitely seen the
bottom in the first quarter itself. And going forward, with higher focus on individual policies, the margin is
going to be towards the upper range of our guidance." Repeated later: "as the product mix normalizes, our
margin will be moving towards the upper end of our band."
GST drag runs off from 22-Sep-2026: "the GST was waived from 22nd of September. So there will be some
impact for 2.5 months in the current quarter also. And then it will be on par-to-par basis" … "even you go to
next quarter, you will see some impact on the GST. And thereafter, we see GST impact will run away."
Product mix — hold, not shift: ULIP 62% / non-ULIP 38% on IRP basis; "For the year also, in fact, our
target is to have this kind of product mix only."
Group business does not repeat: "we are sure that this lumpy kind of business doesn't happen very frequently."
Agency to accelerate: "We are sure that the agency in the remaining 3 quarters will also be contributing
even a stronger number."
61st-month persistency normalises by FY-end: "this cohort will move away from the 61st month by end of
third quarter. So by end of the year, the 61st month persistency, we are expecting will be back to normal."
Other expenses stay elevated, then streamline: "the other expenses will continue in tandem with the sum
assured" … "the next 3 quarters, you will see it will streamline as per the plan."
Credit protect to recover: "it is going as per the planned number. So we will see some good uptick in the
coming quarters."
Regular-pay deferred annuity plan: "Hopefully within next quarter, you will be able to see that" — but a
second management voice immediately hedged: "We are working on the product, and we'll launch the product at
opportune time." (Soft-dated → deliberately NOT logged as a trigger; see §10.)
J&K Bank corporate agency: "the business will be starting sometime in this quarter."
order book & pipeline: Not applicable in the industrial sense — a life insurer's forward book is renewal premium + in-force AUM + the
Renewal premium ₹123.8 bn, +17%, = 58% of GWP — the annuity-like base underneath new business.
AUM ₹5.2 trillion, +10% — the fee/spread earning base.
Embedded value ₹852.9 bn, +15% YoY — the stock of future profit.
Distribution capacity added this quarter: >34,000 agents on a gross basis, 11 new branches,
>60,000 CIFs across SBI + RRBs, and one new corporate-agency tie-up (J&K Bank) yet to start writing.
segment / subsidiary detail: Distribution channels (the real segment axis here):
The GTI segment is the quarter's swing factor: group protection APE ₹12.3bn (+313%), group NBP ₹32.9bn (+41%)
= 37% of NBP. Because GTI is a 1-year renewable contract booked at 100% of premium into APE, it lifts headline
APE growth to +36% while diluting blended margin by 60 bps. Management declined to name the counterparty when an
analyst asked whether it was "related to a certain PSU company".
Riders — a structural change, not a line item. Rider attachment has ramped 35% → 45% → 50%, launched
"1 year back and 1.5 years back, initially, we attached to the traditional product and subsequently moved to the
unit-linked product." Now "almost 45% to 50% policies are being sold along with the rider attachment."
Critically, rider APE is booked into protection, not ULIP: "riders, which is the protection part is taken as
a part of the protection." Management could not quantify rider APE on the call — "Rider APE, we don't have
right now. So we will share with you separately." Explicitly not a high-sum-assured ULIP product:
"we do not have a high sum assured kind of ULIP. We have normal ULIP products in our portfolio."
growth verticals / optionality: Agency scale-up ("Agency 2.0" → "Agency Next") — the 3-year build is now converting: "We have opened more
than 100 branches in last 2 years, last 3 years. And our addition of agents, along with the productivity of
agents has been going up because of the sustained efforts." Agency non-ULIP mix 43%→46% makes this margin-accretive
growth, not just volume.
Non-SBI bancassurance — +31% on APE with a 80% non-ULIP mix, i.e. structurally richer than the SBI
channel. J&K Bank tie-up adds a new corporate agency starting this quarter (not sized on the call → not a
logged trigger).
Pure protection shift — deliberately trading ticket size for margin: ROP:non-ROP moved 73→68:32, pure
protection +52% on IRP basis. Management owned the optics: "22% growth in Individual protection, with 52% pure
protection growth, which is lower ticket size as compared to the ROP. So that is the reason it is showing a
little subdued as compared to the industry. But as far as our plan of actions are concerned, it is going exactly
in that direction."
Non-par savings, actively repriced to the yield curve — "we keep a very sharp eye on the yield movement" …
"And our yields, we keep a close eye and reprice our products as per the yield movement. If you would have
noticed that in the month of June also as per the yield curve movement, we improved IRR for the customers, and
that is also resulting in good traction for this kind of product in the market."
Regular-pay deferred annuity plan — pending launch; annuity + pension new business already ₹18.9bn.
Rider attachment headroom — at ~50% and expected to "improve from this level or maintain to that level."
6a. moat & competitive position: Bancassurance access that cannot be replicated — >60,000 CIFs across SBI + RRBs delivering 47% of
total APE, with SBI branch productivity of ₹4.1 million individual APE per branch (+7%). This is a
distribution asset no private peer can buy.
Scale leadership, held not just claimed — 22.2% private / 15.2% total IRP market share, with a 3-year
IRP CAGR of 14% vs industry 13%, i.e. share gain at scale.
Lowest-cost operator, self-evidenced as a regulatory shield — opex ratio 7.7%, total cost ratio 12%.
Management's answer to the regulatory question rests on this: "we have the lowest surrender, we have the lowest
grievance ratios and also lowest commissions" (analyst framing, accepted) → "we are placed as compared to the
industry in a better position." And on why costs cannot simply be cut to offset GST: "our expenses and the
commission ratio are even on lower side. So we not looking to reduce our expenses or commissions, as they are
already on lower side. What we keep maintaining that our product mix will able to mitigate these things."
Conduct quality as a licence-to-operate moat — misselling ratio 0.02%, "one of the lowest in the
private industry"; death claim settlement 98.8%.
Digital/underwriting throughput — 99.9% of individual proposals submitted digitally; 67% processed
through automated underwriting.
margins & cost dynamics: The VoNB margin bridge management actually gave (component drags, quoted — not summed here):
Product mix: −60 bps, entirely GTI. "This is only on account of the GTI."
GST: −1.1 percentage points. "what you're seeing the 1.1% drag in the margin is on account of GST only."
Assumption change: −40 bps, base effect only (March-'26 annual review, nothing done in Q1; the March
operating-assumption change was itself "negative by 20 basis points").
Reported margin 26.2%; management stated ex-GST margin 27.4% and ex-GST VoNB ₹14.7bn (+35%).
Cost lines rose for two identifiable reasons, both flagged as understood:
1. Stamp duty scales with sum assured — and sum assured is rising by design (riders + protection attachment):
"the sum assured have been increasing for SBI Life significantly. So the stamp duty is corresponding to that …
we are writing good protection business. So plus, in the ULIP in other products also, we are attaching a lot of
protection. So that is the reason the sum assured has been significantly increasing for us. So that gives us
some spike in the other expenses." This is a good-quality cost — it is the price of the mix shift.
2. New labour codes — "the labor code impact to a certain extent because of the number of employees, and this
is the first quarter where we have seen this impact."
Opex ratio 7.7% (vs 6.3%) and total cost ratio 12% (vs 10.8%) reflect both. Management's stance on operating
leverage was notably unpromising: asked why growth doesn't lift margin, the answer was simply that 26–28% "is a
very healthy range of margin" — i.e. surplus is being reinvested, not banked.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Physical/organisational expansion rather than plant capex:
11 new branches added in Q1 FY27; >100 branches opened over the last 2–3 years for the agency build.
>34,000 agents added gross during the quarter.
J&K Bank corporate-agency tie-up — signed in the quarter, "business will be starting sometime in this
quarter" → the slippage item to check next quarter.
Regular-pay deferred annuity product — was "supposed to launch … by end of the quarter" per the analyst,
now "Hopefully within next quarter" / "at opportune time" → already slipping; verify in Q2 FY27.
capital allocation: Solvency 1.96 vs 1.50 regulatory minimum — comfortable headroom; no capital raise, sub-debt, or buyback
was discussed on this call, and no dividend commentary was given.
Capital is being deployed into distribution (agents, branches, bank tie-ups) and product build
Embedded value ₹852.9bn (+15%) is the compounding base; VoNB ₹14.1bn (+29%) is the annual accretion.
Note the absence: unlike peers, no RBC / Ind-AS transition capital commentary was offered this quarter.
risks & watch-items: 1. The margin-recovery promise is the whole thesis now. Management has publicly called the bottom
("we have definitely seen the bottom in the first quarter itself") and guided to the upper end of 26–28%.
That is a falsifiable claim — verify in Q2 FY27.
2. GTI concentration and opacity. A single lumpy group contract moved total APE growth from +14% (individual)
to +36%, and the company refuses to size or name it: "we do not comment on individual contracts."
It is a 1-year renewable contract → renewal risk is a cliff, and the FY28 base is inflated.
3. GST residual through 22-Sep-2026 — 2.5 further months of drag in Q2 FY27 (logged as the trigger, §Trigger).
4. 61st-month persistency deteriorating — the COVID cohort has reached the 61st month. Management expects
normalisation "by end of third quarter" / "by end of the year" — a dated, checkable claim.
5. Individual protection lags peers on the headline. Analysts pushed twice ("why are we like growing a little
bit lower than competition?", "it looks a little weaker compared to the other players"). Management's ROP→pure-term
mix explanation is coherent, but it means reported protection APE growth will stay optically soft.
6. Credit protect is flat — a channel that should benefit from SBI's retail lending is contributing nothing.
7. Cost base structurally higher — stamp duty rises with the (intentional) sum-assured growth, and the labour
code is now permanently in the base.
8. Regulatory uncertainty is unresolved, and management said so — "we will definitely wait and see how this
whole architecture will shape in the near future." No date, no shape → deliberately not logged as a trigger.
9. Deferred annuity launch already slipped once and was hedged twice on this call.
10. Number inconsistencies within the call (record for cross-checking, not adjudicated here): individual
protection growth stated as +18% in prepared remarks but +22% in Q&A; pure protection +41% on
Individual APE basis and +52% on IRP basis; VoNB growth +29% per management vs "30%" per an analyst;
IRP growth 14% per remarks vs "14.5%, 15%" in Q&A.
management quality / tone: Confident and specific, with a notable willingness to be held to dated commitments — the margin bottom, the
61st-month persistency recovery timeline, the GST run-off date, and the FY27 IRP range were all stated without
hedging. Management also self-corrected on air (the other-banks growth figure: "I quoted 31%. It is actually
19% on Individual NBP & 31% on APE basis") and openly refused what it does not disclose rather than
deflecting — "We don't generally discuss product-wise margins. We don't disclose those numbers. So I'll refrain
from that", and "Rider APE, we don't have right now. So we will share with you separately." On the awkward
questions (protection lagging peers, GTI identity, margin drag quantum) the answers were direct or an explicit
decline, not evasion. The one soft spot: management would not engage with the operating-leverage question,
falling back on the guidance band rather than explaining why scale isn't lifting margin.
non-obvious takeaways: 1. The rider strategy quietly relocates margin. Rider APE is booked into protection, not ULIP — so as
attachment ran 35%→45%→50%, part of what looks like "protection growth" is riders sold on ULIP/par policies.
This simultaneously (a) flatters protection metrics, (b) drives the sum-assured surge (+46% individual), and
(c) causes the stamp-duty cost spike management flagged. One decision, three visible effects across three
different sections of the P&L.
2. The reported margin decline is a mix artefact, not deterioration — and the components were given separately.
The −60 bps mix drag was attributed entirely to GTI while par (+35%), non-par (+27%) and pure protection
(+52% IRP) all grew faster than IRP. Strip GTI and the individual book's margin is improving, which is exactly
what the first analyst inferred: "despite GST hit, your individual margins or ex GTI margins have improved
very, very strongly."
3. Total APE (+36%) is the least useful number in the release. Because GTI is a 1-year renewable contract
booked at 100% into APE, the headline APE growth is nearly 2.5x the individual APE growth (+14%). The
management-designated KPI is IRP, deliberately: "as a company, we have always communicated that our focus
is on Individual Rated Premium."
4. Costs are rising for the right reason. The opex ratio deterioration (6.3%→7.7%) is largely stamp duty
scaling with a deliberate sum-assured expansion. A crude cost-ratio screen would read this as inefficiency;
it is the mechanical cost of a better product mix.
5. Being the low-cost, low-misselling operator is being positioned as regulatory optionality. Management's
answer to "what will regulation do?" was to point at lowest surrender / grievance / commission ratios — i.e.
they expect the next regulatory cycle to be relatively accretive to SBI Life, as they claim the last one was:
"the last time also when the regulations were published, and it has actually given us the positive towards the
growth of the industry, including SBI Life."
6. SBI channel growth (+10%) is now the slowest thing in the P&L — agency +20%, other banks +31%, other
channels +160%. Bancassurance dependence is falling by arithmetic rather than by choice, which is margin-positive
(agency and other-bank mixes are richer in non-ULIP) but raises the cost base.
7. The "assumption change −40 bps" line in the VoNB walk is a ghost — no Q1 assumption change was made at all;
it is the March-'26 annual review showing through a June-to-June comparison. Anyone modelling a recurring
assumption drag would be wrong.

near-term trigger (spec §10): GST drag annualises on 22-Sep-2026 — residual ~2.5 months of margin drag in Q2 FY27, then a clean base.
Verbatim: "So the GST was waived from 22nd of September. So there will be some impact for 2.5 months in the
current quarter also. And then it will be on par-to-par basis." Reinforced: "even you go to next quarter, you
will see some impact on the GST. And thereafter, we see GST impact will run away."
Size as stated by management (not computed here): "The GST impact for the quarter is INR2.3 billion";
"Excluding GST impact, VoNB would have been INR14.7 billion, representing 35% growth with a VoNB margin of 27.4%"
against a reported 26.2% — i.e. a stated 1.1 pp margin drag against a guided band of only 26–28%.
Type Margin/Price · Timing 22-Sep-2026 (within Q2 FY27, Jul–Sep 2026) · Impact Medium vs SBI Life's own size.
Considered and deliberately EXCLUDED (fail the hard-dated and/or High/Medium-vs-own-size test):
J&K Bank corporate-agency go-live — "the business will be starting sometime in this quarter": dated but
"sometime", and entirely unsized against ₹53.8bn quarterly APE / 60,000 SBI CIFs → Low.
Regular-pay deferred annuity launch — "Hopefully within next quarter" immediately hedged by "we'll launch
the product at opportune time"; already slipped once; unsized → soft-dated, Low.
Margin recovery to the upper band — an FY27 directional guide, not hard-dated to the next 3 months.
61st-month persistency normalisation — dated to "end of third quarter" / FY-end, i.e. beyond the ~3-month
window, and a metric-optics recovery rather than a P&L event.
Regulatory architecture — explicitly undated: "we will definitely wait and see."
qoq change log (fill each quarter): Q1 FY27 (this): First note for SBILIFE — no prior quarter in output/concall/ to diff against. IRP ₹39.7bn
(+14%) and VoNB ₹14.1bn (+29%) delivered in line with the 14–15% IRP guide, but reported VoNB margin 26.2%
landed at the lower end of the 26–28% band on a one-off GTI mix drag (−60 bps) plus GST (−1.1 pp).
Management called the margin bottom and reaffirmed 26–28% trending to the upper end. Mix genuinely
improving: ULIP 62% of IRP (vs 65% contribution in Q1 FY26), pure protection +41% (Ind. APE) / +52% (IRP),
ROP:non-ROP 73→68:32, rider attachment ~50%. Agency +20%, other banks +31% (APE), SBI banca +10%. Solvency 1.96,
AUM ₹5.2tn, EV ₹852.9bn. Cost ratios stepped up (opex 6.3%→7.7%) on stamp duty + labour codes. New: J&K Bank
corporate agency signed.
Q2 FY27 → check: (1) did VoNB margin move OFF 26.2% toward the upper band, as promised? (2) GTI — does group
APE collapse back to ~10–12% of total, and does the 1-yr contract renew? (3) GST residual — only 2.5 months of
drag, then clean? (4) J&K Bank business actually started? (5) deferred annuity plan launched, or slipped again?
(6) 61st-month persistency — cohort out by end-Q3 as guided? (7) credit protect — the promised "good uptick"?
(8) opex ratio — did other expenses "streamline as per the plan"? (9) IRP growth still in the 14–15% range?

noticed that in the month of June also as per the yield curve movement, we improved IRR for the customers, and
that is also resulting in good traction for this kind of product in the market."
Regular-pay deferred annuity plan — pending launch; annuity + pension new business already ₹18.9bn.
Rider attachment headroom — at ~50% and expected to "improve from this level or maintain to that level."
6a. moat & competitive position: Bancassurance access that cannot be replicated — >60,000 CIFs across SBI + RRBs delivering 47% of
total APE, with SBI branch productivity of ₹4.1 million individual APE per branch (+7%). This is a
distribution asset no private peer can buy.
Scale leadership, held not just claimed — 22.2% private / 15.2% total IRP market share, with a 3-year
IRP CAGR of 14% vs industry 13%, i.e. share gain at scale.
Lowest-cost operator, self-evidenced as a regulatory shield — opex ratio 7.7%, total cost ratio 12%.
Management's answer to the regulatory question rests on this: "we have the lowest surrender, we have the lowest
grievance ratios and also lowest commissions" (analyst framing, accepted) → "we are placed as compared to the
industry in a better position." And on why costs cannot simply be cut to offset GST: "our expenses and the
commission ratio are even on lower side. So we not looking to reduce our expenses or commissions, as they are
already on lower side. What we keep maintaining that our product mix will able to mitigate these things."
Conduct quality as a licence-to-operate moat — misselling ratio 0.02%, "one of the lowest in the
private industry"; death claim settlement 98.8%.
Digital/underwriting throughput — 99.9% of individual proposals submitted digitally; 67% processed
through automated underwriting.
margins & cost dynamics: The VoNB margin bridge management actually gave (component drags, quoted — not summed here):
Product mix: −60 bps, entirely GTI. "This is only on account of the GTI."
GST: −1.1 percentage points. "what you're seeing the 1.1% drag in the margin is on account of GST only."
Assumption change: −40 bps, base effect only (March-'26 annual review, nothing done in Q1; the March
operating-assumption change was itself "negative by 20 basis points").
Reported margin 26.2%; management stated ex-GST margin 27.4% and ex-GST VoNB ₹14.7bn (+35%).
Cost lines rose for two identifiable reasons, both flagged as understood:
1. Stamp duty scales with sum assured — and sum assured is rising by design (riders + protection attachment):
"the sum assured have been increasing for SBI Life significantly. So the stamp duty is corresponding to that …
we are writing good protection business. So plus, in the ULIP in other products also, we are attaching a lot of
protection. So that is the reason the sum assured has been significantly increasing for us. So that gives us
some spike in the other expenses." This is a good-quality cost — it is the price of the mix shift.
2. New labour codes — "the labor code impact to a certain extent because of the number of employees, and this
is the first quarter where we have seen this impact."
Opex ratio 7.7% (vs 6.3%) and total cost ratio 12% (vs 10.8%) reflect both. Management's stance on operating
leverage was notably unpromising: asked why growth doesn't lift margin, the answer was simply that 26–28% "is a
very healthy range of margin" — i.e. surplus is being reinvested, not banked.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Physical/organisational expansion rather than plant capex:
11 new branches added in Q1 FY27; >100 branches opened over the last 2–3 years for the agency build.
>34,000 agents added gross during the quarter.
J&K Bank corporate-agency tie-up — signed in the quarter, "business will be starting sometime in this
quarter" → the slippage item to check next quarter.
Regular-pay deferred annuity product — was "supposed to launch … by end of the quarter" per the analyst,
now "Hopefully within next quarter" / "at opportune time" → already slipping; verify in Q2 FY27.
capital allocation: Solvency 1.96 vs 1.50 regulatory minimum — comfortable headroom; no capital raise, sub-debt, or buyback
was discussed on this call, and no dividend commentary was given.
Capital is being deployed into distribution (agents, branches, bank tie-ups) and product build
Embedded value ₹852.9bn (+15%) is the compounding base; VoNB ₹14.1bn (+29%) is the annual accretion.
Note the absence: unlike peers, no RBC / Ind-AS transition capital commentary was offered this quarter.
risks & watch-items: 1. The margin-recovery promise is the whole thesis now. Management has publicly called the bottom
("we have definitely seen the bottom in the first quarter itself") and guided to the upper end of 26–28%.
That is a falsifiable claim — verify in Q2 FY27.
2. GTI concentration and opacity. A single lumpy group contract moved total APE growth from +14% (individual)
to +36%, and the company refuses to size or name it: "we do not comment on individual contracts."
It is a 1-year renewable contract → renewal risk is a cliff, and the FY28 base is inflated.
3. GST residual through 22-Sep-2026 — 2.5 further months of drag in Q2 FY27 (logged as the trigger, §Trigger).
4. 61st-month persistency deteriorating — the COVID cohort has reached the 61st month. Management expects
normalisation "by end of third quarter" / "by end of the year" — a dated, checkable claim.
5. Individual protection lags peers on the headline. Analysts pushed twice ("why are we like growing a little
bit lower than competition?", "it looks a little weaker compared to the other players"). Management's ROP→pure-term
mix explanation is coherent, but it means reported protection APE growth will stay optically soft.
6. Credit protect is flat — a channel that should benefit from SBI's retail lending is contributing nothing.
7. Cost base structurally higher — stamp duty rises with the (intentional) sum-assured growth, and the labour
code is now permanently in the base.
8. Regulatory uncertainty is unresolved, and management said so — "we will definitely wait and see how this
whole architecture will shape in the near future." No date, no shape → deliberately not logged as a trigger.
9. Deferred annuity launch already slipped once and was hedged twice on this call.
10. Number inconsistencies within the call (record for cross-checking, not adjudicated here): individual
protection growth stated as +18% in prepared remarks but +22% in Q&A; pure protection +41% on
Individual APE basis and +52% on IRP basis; VoNB growth +29% per management vs "30%" per an analyst;
IRP growth 14% per remarks vs "14.5%, 15%" in Q&A.
management quality / tone: Confident and specific, with a notable willingness to be held to dated commitments — the margin bottom, the
61st-month persistency recovery timeline, the GST run-off date, and the FY27 IRP range were all stated without
hedging. Management also self-corrected on air (the other-banks growth figure: "I quoted 31%. It is actually
19% on Individual NBP & 31% on APE basis") and openly refused what it does not disclose rather than
deflecting — "We don't generally discuss product-wise margins. We don't disclose those numbers. So I'll refrain
from that", and "Rider APE, we don't have right now. So we will share with you separately." On the awkward
questions (protection lagging peers, GTI identity, margin drag quantum) the answers were direct or an explicit
decline, not evasion. The one soft spot: management would not engage with the operating-leverage question,
falling back on the guidance band rather than explaining why scale isn't lifting margin.
non-obvious takeaways: 1. The rider strategy quietly relocates margin. Rider APE is booked into protection, not ULIP — so as
attachment ran 35%→45%→50%, part of what looks like "protection growth" is riders sold on ULIP/par policies.
This simultaneously (a) flatters protection metrics, (b) drives the sum-assured surge (+46% individual), and
(c) causes the stamp-duty cost spike management flagged. One decision, three visible effects across three
different sections of the P&L.
2. The reported margin decline is a mix artefact, not deterioration — and the components were given separately.
The −60 bps mix drag was attributed entirely to GTI while par (+35%), non-par (+27%) and pure protection
(+52% IRP) all grew faster than IRP. Strip GTI and the individual book's margin is improving, which is exactly
what the first analyst inferred: "despite GST hit, your individual margins or ex GTI margins have improved
very, very strongly."
3. Total APE (+36%) is the least useful number in the release. Because GTI is a 1-year renewable contract
booked at 100% into APE, the headline APE growth is nearly 2.5x the individual APE growth (+14%). The
management-designated KPI is IRP, deliberately: "as a company, we have always communicated that our focus
is on Individual Rated Premium."
4. Costs are rising for the right reason. The opex ratio deterioration (6.3%→7.7%) is largely stamp duty
scaling with a deliberate sum-assured expansion. A crude cost-ratio screen would read this as inefficiency;
it is the mechanical cost of a better product mix.
5. Being the low-cost, low-misselling operator is being positioned as regulatory optionality. Management's
answer to "what will regulation do?" was to point at lowest surrender / grievance / commission ratios — i.e.
they expect the next regulatory cycle to be relatively accretive to SBI Life, as they claim the last one was:
"the last time also when the regulations were published, and it has actually given us the positive towards the
growth of the industry, including SBI Life."
6. SBI channel growth (+10%) is now the slowest thing in the P&L — agency +20%, other banks +31%, other
channels +160%. Bancassurance dependence is falling by arithmetic rather than by choice, which is margin-positive
(agency and other-bank mixes are richer in non-ULIP) but raises the cost base.
7. The "assumption change −40 bps" line in the VoNB walk is a ghost — no Q1 assumption change was made at all;
it is the March-'26 annual review showing through a June-to-June comparison. Anyone modelling a recurring
assumption drag would be wrong.

near-term trigger (spec §10): GST drag annualises on 22-Sep-2026 — residual ~2.5 months of margin drag in Q2 FY27, then a clean base.
Verbatim: "So the GST was waived from 22nd of September. So there will be some impact for 2.5 months in the
current quarter also. And then it will be on par-to-par basis." Reinforced: "even you go to next quarter, you
will see some impact on the GST. And thereafter, we see GST impact will run away."
Size as stated by management (not computed here): "The GST impact for the quarter is INR2.3 billion";
"Excluding GST impact, VoNB would have been INR14.7 billion, representing 35% growth with a VoNB margin of 27.4%"
against a reported 26.2% — i.e. a stated 1.1 pp margin drag against a guided band of only 26–28%.
Type Margin/Price · Timing 22-Sep-2026 (within Q2 FY27, Jul–Sep 2026) · Impact Medium vs SBI Life's own size.
Considered and deliberately EXCLUDED (fail the hard-dated and/or High/Medium-vs-own-size test):
J&K Bank corporate-agency go-live — "the business will be starting sometime in this quarter": dated but
"sometime", and entirely unsized against ₹53.8bn quarterly APE / 60,000 SBI CIFs → Low.
Regular-pay deferred annuity launch — "Hopefully within next quarter" immediately hedged by "we'll launch
the product at opportune time"; already slipped once; unsized → soft-dated, Low.
Margin recovery to the upper band — an FY27 directional guide, not hard-dated to the next 3 months.
61st-month persistency normalisation — dated to "end of third quarter" / FY-end, i.e. beyond the ~3-month
window, and a metric-optics recovery rather than a P&L event.
Regulatory architecture — explicitly undated: "we will definitely wait and see."
qoq change log (fill each quarter): Q1 FY27 (this): First note for SBILIFE — no prior quarter in output/concall/ to diff against. IRP ₹39.7bn
(+14%) and VoNB ₹14.1bn (+29%) delivered in line with the 14–15% IRP guide, but reported VoNB margin 26.2%
landed at the lower end of the 26–28% band on a one-off GTI mix drag (−60 bps) plus GST (−1.1 pp).
Management called the margin bottom and reaffirmed 26–28% trending to the upper end. Mix genuinely
improving: ULIP 62% of IRP (vs 65% contribution in Q1 FY26), pure protection +41% (Ind. APE) / +52% (IRP),
ROP:non-ROP 73→68:32, rider attachment ~50%. Agency +20%, other banks +31% (APE), SBI banca +10%. Solvency 1.96,
AUM ₹5.2tn, EV ₹852.9bn. Cost ratios stepped up (opex 6.3%→7.7%) on stamp duty + labour codes. New: J&K Bank
corporate agency signed.
Q2 FY27 → check: (1) did VoNB margin move OFF 26.2% toward the upper band, as promised? (2) GTI — does group
APE collapse back to ~10–12% of total, and does the 1-yr contract renew? (3) GST residual — only 2.5 months of
drag, then clean? (4) J&K Bank business actually started? (5) deferred annuity plan launched, or slipped again?
(6) 61st-month persistency — cohort out by end-Q3 as guided? (7) credit protect — the promised "good uptick"?
(8) opex ratio — did other expenses "streamline as per the plan"? (9) IRP growth still in the 14–15% range?
